messages.subject: scantwo plot interpretation
parts:
I am a novice in QTL in general, so I may be asking a really stupid
question here.

My first run on R/qtl resulted in a scantwo plot (bottom right),
yellow-colored all the way cross on a locus with the matchpoint for
red. Does it mean that I have a single locus affecting the phenotype?
I am still wondering why the locus has interaction (yellow) all across
the genomic region.

If anybody can help me out, I would appreciate it tremendously.

messages.author: 5523cb16ec47d553
messages.subject: Re: scantwo plot interpretation
parts:
Hi Euny,

By default, the lower right of the scantwo plot shows full LOD
scores. This means the display is of evidence for a two-QTL +
interaction model, over the null model. It sounds like you have a
single locus of very large effect, so that any full model containing
this locus has a strong signal. I would advise you to look closely at
your scanone plot, and then try to understand the scantwo plot in
light of those results.

Regards,
Ani
